newsitem.title: INDIA: GOLD - Demand slump hits Indian sub-continent.
newsitem.headline: GOLD - Demand slump hits Indian sub-continent.

text.p: Gold demand is slumping in the Indian sub-continent with traders in India and Pakistan reporting little business, dealers said on Monday.
Dealers in Bombay said demand for gold remained poor and smuggling was further depressing prices.

"Arrivals of smuggled gold by sea were high last week but are expected to slow down once monsoon rains start," said Babubhai Jain, a leading bullion dealer. A monsoon is expected to hit Bombay this week.
Gold is smuggled into India by sea on small boats plying between India and the Gulf.
In Pakistan, gold is expected to move in a narrow band after the government ruled out a devaluation of its currency in last week's budget for 1997/98.
Dealers in the Gulf trading hub of Dubai said expatriate Indians returning home for summer holidays were expected to buy gold and jewellery as gifts to take back home.
Dubai feeds gold demand from India, the world's largest consumer of the metal, and its neighbour Pakistan. The two supply a huge number of expatriate workers to the Gulf.
In Bombay, gold prices fell by 40 rupees per 10 grams to 4,640 rupees in the week to Monday. The previous week they had shed 90 rupees.
Dealers said premiums on acquiring special import licences for importing gold had also come down to 10 percent from around 14 percent a month ago, indicating slack demand for imports.
"Since domestic prices are low, there's not much incentive for importing gold," said a bullion dealer.
Dealers said an international jewellery fair organised in the last week of June should cheer the bullion traders, though it was meant to boost exports.

"As one of the world's fastest growing jewellery centres, India is becoming an important destination on the itineraries of buyers worldwide," said Praveen Pandya, chairman of the Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council, sponsors of the fair.
Dealers in Karachi, Pakistan's main commercial centre, said they would expect gold prices to fluctuate in a narrow band on speculative buying in the current week.
On the Karachi bullion market, gold prices fell 47 rupees to 4,638 rupees per 10 grams in the week to Saturday.

In Dubai, dealers on Sunday said they pinned their hopes for a pick-up in local retail trade on expatriates, mostly from the Indian sub-continent, returning home for the summer holidays laden with gifts.
As many of Dubai's expatriate community began to head for home or vacations abroad to escape the Gulf summer, traders expected an upturn in sales.
"Expatriates, particularly my Indian clients, are starting to buy gifts for family members. Dubai offers a good deal," a trader at one of Dubai's main jewellery houses said.
Weaker bullion prices were also expected to help demand as the annual holiday exodus began, dealers said.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMS in U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $1=35.81 Indian rupees, 40.49 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams) *Bombay prices June 16/9, Karachi June 14/7 and Dubai June 15/8.
